review_comments.body:
I was recently made aware of https://github.com/NixOS/rfcs/blob/master/rfcs/0042-config-option.md#part-2-balancing-module-option-count from https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/554366#discussion_r3842780480

Do you think all the options here are needed? Only the important ones are useful.

In nixpkgs there is an experimental way to write modules, maybe you have come across them, called modular services. https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/README-modular-services.md
If you are interested we can turn this module into a modular service, which comes with a good UX for running multiple instances of the same service, among other things.

Let me know if you are interested in porting this to a modular service, or I am happy to adapt this PR while keeping your ownership and giving you the proper credit.

I will respect your decision if you think we should not pursue it for this module at all, so don't feel pressured into using them.

review_comments.body:
A slightly more useful test here would be a smoke test, unless opengist already does e2e tests during the building of its package derivation, in which case a curl health check is good enough.

I'm thinking the smoke test should create an account, then login to opengist, create a gist, clone it via ssh as well as http and check that files cloned match.
Could be `gitMinimal` but I think `git` is good.
